narrative.overview:
Everything is where a Hevy user's hand already goes. The layout starts from Hevy's on purpose: its set table, its page bar, its list of finished workouts. The skin is OpenBite's (D123): Nunito, warm greys, round shapes, each exercise in its own card on a pure black page. A new screen is right when someone who trained with Hevy for years finds every control where they expect it, and someone who uses OpenBite knows the look.

The mood is dark, calm and dense. Rows stay compact, parts are split by hairlines, and there is no decoration. The numbers are the content. Cards are black with a hairline drawn inside, not grey slabs, so the page stays one black surface and the cards read as outlines on it. Buttons and chips are full pills; set values sit in small rounded wells; ticks are circles.

It is not upstream openGym's iOS look: no large titles, no tinted icon tiles, no Apple system colours. It is not a gamified fitness app either: no gradients, no glow, no badges, no confetti, no hero numbers for show. Control sizes are Hevy's; D123 changed the skin, not the hit targets.
keyCharacteristics: A pure black page. An exercise in a workout, a finished workout, Today's next session and its last workout each sit in a black card with a hairline. Lists of exercises and routines run flat between hairlines; fills are kept for controls, wells and stat tiles.
One accent, which the user chooses. It means "tap this", "this is next" and "this is done".
The other colours carry meanings (warm-up, failure, drop set, superset, cardio, deload, record, note), and each steps aside when the accent or another meaning comes too close.
Warm greys and warm white text, never cool blue-greys.
Tabular numbers everywhere, so a column of sets lines up, and one way of writing a set.
One page bar on every screen: a bare chevron, a small centred title, plain actions.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: The accent is the only colour that means "tap", "next" or "done". A thing that is none of those never wears it.

rules.name: The Step Aside Rule
rules.body: A meaning colour never takes the accent's place. When the user's accent, or another meaning, is too close to one, the meaning moves to its backup or an extra hue; done and "better than last time" always wear the accent.

rules.name: The Earned Colour Rule
rules.body: Meaning colours show up because something is so: a set was warm-up, failed or dropped, a record fell, a day was cardio. They never decorate a resting screen.

rules.name: The Grey Until Touched Rule
rules.body: A value the app filled in is faint grey and medium weight. It turns white and bold once it is typed or its set is ticked (D2). The opened set is the one exception: its prefilled values are already white and bold, since they are what you lift now (D127).

rules.name: The No Large Title Rule
rules.body: A page names itself in the 17px bar. Nothing on a page is set above 22px except a number you act on now: the opened set's values, the rest countdown, the plan keypad's value, the strap's live readouts (D127).

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Any number that can change or sit in a column uses tabular figures.

rules.name: The One Set Format Rule
rules.body: A set is written one way everywhere: "80 × 8", spaced. Where no KG or LB column head names the unit, it comes once, after the weight: "80 kg × 8". Repeats lead with their count, "2 × 80 × 8, 80 × 7". PREVIOUS in the live table carries no unit, since its column head does. Only the share cards keep Hevy's "80kg × 8 reps".

rules.name: The Flat At Rest Rule
rules.body: Nothing casts a shadow. Every box-shadow in the fork's CSS is inset, a line, or the one sticky fade.

dos: **Do** put a new screen's title in the one page bar: bare chevron, centred 17px/700, plain actions (D49).
**Do** put an exercise in a workout, or a finished workout, in a black 26px card with the card hairline (`--hv-card-line`), and let its rows run to the card's edges.
**Do** list exercises and routines as flat rows split by hairlines.
**Do** write every set through `setFormat` or `setRuns`: "80 × 8", the unit once where no column head names it.
**Do** draw the accent from `--acc`, `--acc-2` and `--on-acc`, never from a hex: the user chooses it.
**Do** read a meaning colour from its `--hv-*` variable (`var(--hv-warmup, var(--yellow))`), so it steps aside from the accent.

**Do** draw with the tokens in `theme.css` (`--bg`, `--surface`, `--surface-2`, `--surface-3`, `--label`, `--label-2`, `--label-3`, `--sep`, `--r-sm`, `--r`, `--r-card`, `--r-xl`), scoped under `:root[data-ui="hevier"]`.
**Do** head a part of a page with a 13px grey section heading (h2, or h3 under an h2).
**Do** keep every target at 44px by extending it invisibly, not by making the control bigger.
**Do** set every changing number in tabular figures.
**Do** keep the faint grey (`--label-3`) at 4.5:1 on the opened set's row.
donts: **Don't** bring back upstream's iOS look: large titles, tinted icon tiles, filled circles behind header icons, Apple's system colours.
**Don't** add what a gamified fitness app has: gradients, glow, badges, confetti, big numbers for decoration.
**Don't** give anything a drop shadow; an edge is a hairline.
**Don't** fill a danger button red or tint it; red is its text on well grey.
**Don't** set an accent value in `theme.css`: it would beat every pick (D123).
**Don't** add a preset accent that sits under 0.12 OKLab from a meaning colour or another preset.
**Don't** offer a light theme (D17). The light token block exists only for upstream's timer flash.
**Don't** use cool blue-greys; the greys are warm.
**Don't** add a second typeface, or set anything above 22px that is not a number you act on now.
**Don't** outline a card, a chip or a field with a CSS border; a card's edge is the inset hairline, a title field's the hairline under it.
**Don't** write a set as "80kg x 8" or "80×8", or repeat the unit under a KG or LB head.
